chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfali, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Hashemi, from Abu Khalid Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from a man, from Ibn al-Munkadir via his chain, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The best of you are those who feed food, spread greetings, and pray while people are asleep.

key_terms.صَلَّى: prayed (specifically night prayer in this context)

ai.seo_question: What are the three best deeds mentioned in this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq includes this hadith in 'The Best Three People' to illustrate the integration of social etiquette (adab) with spiritual discipline, a hallmark of Shia ethical teachings. The emphasis on praying while others are asleep highlights the virtue of *Qiyam al-Layl* as a distinct marker of piety, while feeding others and spreading Salam foster communal cohesion (ta'awun). This triad reflects the Shia ideal of balancing individual worship with active social responsibility.
